name: Satyr Hooves
summary: In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek sends warriors north for Satyr Hooves. He needs their strange power to forge brutal gauntlets.

sections.title: Harnessing Corrupted Essence
sections.body: Ula'elek sends you into Ashenvale's ancient woods to gather what his craft requires. Demonic corruption still clings to the satyr covens there, and he seeks more than iron and leather for armor meant to rival Kalimdor's fiercest forces.

sections.title: The Bloat of Ashenvale's Magic
sections.body: In northeastern Ashenvale, satyrs feed on the forest's lingering purity and twist it into foul power. Those that take in the most develop swollen hooves without the usual cloven split. Ula'elek plans to draw out that concentrated magic and weave it into the gauntlets he makes.

faq.q: Why does Ula'elek need satyr hooves?
faq.answer: Ula'elek needs the hooves to empower the brutal gauntlets he is making. He means to draw out the forest magic the satyrs have drained and corrupted.
Satyrs dwell in northeastern Ashenvale, among corrupted ancient ruins, where they drain the deep forest's lingering magic.

faq.q: What makes an uncloven hoof special?
faq.answer: A hoof without a cloven split marks a satyr that has gorged itself on Ashenvale's pure magic. The stolen power swells its feet.
Ula'elek is a skilled Darkspear troll armor craftsman in Sen'jin Village, in southern Durotar. He helps warriors craft trial gear.
Ula'elek is preparing a pair of Brutal Gauntlets, heavy hand armor imbued with stolen magic for rising Horde warriors.

faq.q: Do the satyrs serve the Burning Legion here?
faq.answer: Yes. Satyrs are ancient night elves transformed by demonic pacts. The covens lingering in Kalimdor's woodlands still wield fel corruption in service to demonic powers.

angles.text: As a warrior, you face cunning demonic ambushers as part of your rite of progression. The trial tests your martial resilience and earns you personalized armor.
As a Horde warrior, you leave Durotar's arid plains and travel deep into contested night elf territory in Ashenvale.
As a troll, you can see Darkspear craft in Ula'elek's methods: he draws raw essence from fallen magical foes instead of relying only on conventional smithing.
